title: Classification of the whole working tree against the bound write scope
method: Every path from git status --porcelain -uall, with untracked directories expanded to files, matched against the writeScopes of the bound slice. Nothing is judged from memory.

outsideWriteScope.finding: The lead is right. Two files were changed without an effective scope authorization, both under tests/ViciOne.ServiceBus.EntityFrameworkCoreIntegration.Tests, which is the only test project of this repository that the writeScopes do not list.
outsideWriteScope.when: Both after record 0017, during the entity-framework work.
outsideWriteScope.howItHappened: The re-slice named entity-framework as part of the remaining set Team 1 closes, and I read that as covering the edits the closure needs. It does not: the task text does not widen writeScopes. I did not check the scope list before editing.
outsideWriteScope.gateEffect: None. Until a valid re-slice these two files carry no gate or release effect, and neither does any result that depends on them.

dependentResults.note: What these two files actually carry, so the lead can separate preliminary work from releasable evidence.
dependentResults.entityFrameworkGate: Depends on both files. Without them the category is not green: PostgresTestDbParameters carries the run-scoped PostgreSQL endpoint, and TransactionalBusOutbox_Specs carries the per test expectation that removes the shared task across its three tests.
dependentResults.requirementMatrix: The all-green matrix depends on the entity-framework gate and is therefore preliminary as a whole.
notDependent: core: the two corrections sit in tests/ViciOne.ServiceBus.Tests and src/ViciOne.ServiceBus.TestFramework, both inside the write scope
rabbitmq, activemq, analyzer, abstractions, policy and pack: no file outside the write scope is involved
